Grid division reuse review (read-only)
Worktree /home/wishapig/hackathon-overnight/grid_division, baseP010 b80e04d5e68ba5b8427955d55d4fd5b1ec1589e0; src/graph.cpp first grid-discovery pass only,12 additions/8 deletions. No code changes, compile, numerical run, graph execution or benchmark by reviewer.

Conclusion: no blocking semantic, divisor, overflow, fallback or multi-buffer issue found. Candidate removes redundant first-pass identity calculation using already needed geometric quotients. Whether compiler output and full score improve is owner's/root's measurement task.

Guards and empty domains:
- Original work.tick remains exactly once before each region. rows0 orcols0 still skips before anydivision. Empty stride0 regions thus remain skipped, not divided or newly rejected.
- Nonempty regions check stride0 andcols>stride before computing columns=stride/cols. Because cols>0 from skip andstride>0 fromguard, all divisors safe.
- stride%cols mismatch still returnsfalse. The new columns quotient computed just before that check cannot throw or mutate state.
- row=offset/stride andcol=offset%stride safe for any unsignedsize_t offset. tile_row=row/rows andtile_col=col/cols safe because rows/cols>0. Their remainder alignment checks still reject nonorigin-aligned rectangularaccess. Computing a quotient before its remainder check has no exception or mutable side effect.

Identity equivalence:
New ID=checked_add(checked_mul(tile_row,columns),tile_col) with tile_row=(offset/stride)/rows, columns=stride/cols, tile_col=(offset%stride)/cols. This is exactly oldcell(r,g) when ggeometrymatchesr.
Fornewbuffer, g is populated fromr andcolumns; old andnewcell operands identical. Foranexistingbuffer, rows/cols/stride equality is checked before newcheckedID, so usingr-derivedquotients equalsusinggfields. Differentbuffer names still choose independent grids throughunchangedfind_grid stringequality. No pointeridentity or Cholesky-specific reasoning.

Exception and fallback order:
- accesses checkedincrement remains after geometryproof beforefind_grid.
- Newgrid grow andpush_back still happen beforecheckedID; thus existing allocation/resource failure priority is unchanged.
- Existinggrid mismatch still returnsfalse beforecheckedmul/add. The oldbuilder would decline fastpath instead of raisingIDoverflow; newcode retains that distinction. Only safeunsignedquotient computations moved earlier.
- Checkedmul/add helpers unchanged, soactualoverflow still ordinary graphsizeoverflow, notmisclassifiedResourceLimit. ResourceLimit/bad_alloc fastpathfallback remainsunchanged.

State/budget:
first/last minmax unchanged; dense cellcount,last-first+1,base offsets, sparse fallback, states/readers/edges/deps storage unchanged. Noextraarray orretainedbytes, no extra default cap, no changedtick ormaxsteps semantics. Secondaccesspass stillusesoldcell andsameggeometry. Graph edges/indegrees/output semantics unaffected.

Limits:
This is the currentuncommitted snapshot; exactcandidatecommit and existingendpointacceptance must be retained byowner/root. No runtime performanceclaim fromsourcealone. Reviewdoesnot request extraaudit/guards orpermanenttests.
